parameters.name: update_page
parameters.description: Update title and/or body of a page or blogpost by REPLACING the content. To add an entry to a list or a row to a table, use append_to_page instead: it does not rewrite the page and cannot lose existing content. Body must be storage-format HTML. The version is bumped automatically. Best practice: call get_page first and pass its Version as expected_version - the update is then refused instead of silently overwriting someone else's edit. Content that exists only in ADF format (no storage representation) is refused rather than wiped. Sending only a title keeps the existing body. Parameters: page_id (required), title (optional), body (optional), expected_version (optional), change_note (optional), content_type (optional). A new body that is much shorter than the current one is refused, because that usually means formatting or other entries were lost; pass allow_shrink=true if it is intended.

value.expected_version: ={{ $fromAI('expected_version', 'Optional but recommended: the version number get_page reported. The update is refused if the content changed in the meantime.', 'string') }}
value.change_note: ={{ $fromAI('change_note', 'Optional short note for the Confluence version history, e.g. who asked for the change.', 'string') }}
value.content_type: ={{ $fromAI('content_type', 'Optional: page or blogpost. Leave empty to auto-detect.', 'string') }}
value.allow_shrink: ={{ $fromAI('allow_shrink', 'Set to true only if the new body is deliberately much shorter than the current one. Without it a large shrink is refused.', 'string') }}

parameters.name: append_to_page
parameters.description: Append content to an existing page or blogpost WITHOUT rewriting it. This is the right tool for adding an entry to a list or a row to a table, for example a feedback log. Only the new part is sent, the existing content is untouched, so nothing can get lost and the page keeps its formatting. Use update_page only when existing content really has to change. Parameters: page_id (required), cells (JSON array of strings for a new table row, escaping is handled for you), html (alternative: a storage-format snippet such as a paragraph), location (optional: table appends into the last table, end appends at the bottom of the page), change_note (optional), expected_version (optional), content_type (optional).
